title: Petrol price relief on the cards for December, but diesel motorists face a different story - IOL
text:
Petrol price relief on the cards for December, but diesel motorists face a different story Business Economy Petrol price relief on the cards for December, but diesel motorists face a different story
 Jason Woosey | Published 1 hour ago Ask AI 2 min Petrol prices could plunge in December, but diesel motorists may face another increase 
 Image: Gemini
 The balance of probabilities is swinging sharply towards significant petrol price cuts in December; the news isn't as rosy for diesel customers. 
 The latest data from the Central Energy Fund implies that motorists could see price cuts of R2.62 for 95 Unleaded and R2.35 for 93 Unleaded, even after factoring in the 50 cents that will be added to the equation after Treasury's temporary fuel tax reprieve is scaled back. 
 Diesel motorists face the return of R1.50 to the General Fuel Levy, with current data pointing to price increases of between 16 cents (50ppm) and 53 cents (500ppm) once this is factored in. However, if current trends persist, the diesel over-recovery could grow further between now and month-end, potentially even resulting in a small price reduction.
 Cheaper fuel is certainly emerging as a very realistic possibility for December; however, there is a big caveat, as any escalation of conflict in the Middle East could see oil prices rising rapidly once again. 
 The more positive fuel price data that we've spoken of is a direct result of lower international oil prices, with benchmark Brent crude having tumbled by around 15% following major Republican losses in the US midterm elections, settling below the $100 per barrel mark this week. 
 “Brent crude is holding near $98/barrel, marginally softer, after US President Donald Trump signalled fresh Iran strikes are unlikely should talks progress, draining some of oil’s risk premium,” said Bianca Botes, managing director at Citadel Global. 
 However, Investec chief economist Annabel Bishop cautioned that the longer-term outlook for transport costs remains clouded by current realities and near-term hurdles. 
 “Freight rates rose to record highs last month for oil shipping, with oil stocks very low and little near-term chance of rebuilding inventories. Transport costs for tankers are at record highs, while other logistics costs such as insurance have climbed steeply.” 
 The projected fuel price cuts also arrive at a time when South Africans are paying record prices for petrol and diesel. 
 While the beginning of November saw petrol prices cut by one cent and diesel by between R1.10 and R1.20, petrol has risen by almost R10 per litre this year, while diesel has gone up by around R13, after the US war on Iran created extreme volatility in international oil markets.
